subsection.name: Writing the Controller
subsection.p: The controller is the object which binds the model and the view together.
For a Swing application, create a subclass of org.scopemvc.controller.basic.BasicController to use as the controller for the panel (=view) you are creating.

subsection.name: Issuing controls
subsection.p:
Controls are the equivalent of events in traditional Swing programming.
Most SComponents, which are subclasses of standard Swing components, will issue a Control to the bound Controller instead of firing an event to their listeners.

The code becomes cleaner because the code responding to user events will always be put in the Controller, and not in the View. There are limits also with this approach as not all Swing events are converted to Controls, but you can always write a listener to those events that will issue a Control.
